cluster_genes.affinage_functional_annotation: B3GNT2 is the principal polylactosamine synthase in mammals, catalyzing β1,3-N-acetylglucosamine transfer to extend poly-N-acetyllactosamine chains on N-glycans of diverse cell-surface glycoproteins. Crystal structures in multiple ligand-bound states reveal a sequential kinetic mechanism, with an N-terminal helical domain that contributes to acceptor substrate discrimination and active-site residues whose mutation abolishes catalytic activity [PMID:33158990]. B3gnt2-knockout mice demonstrate dramatically reduced polylactosamine on N-glycans and hyperactivation of T and B cells due to loss of polylactosamine on co-receptors CD28 and CD19, establishing the enzyme as a negative regulator of lymphocyte activation [PMID:20816167]. In cancer, B3GNT2-mediated polylactosamine extension on multiple tumor-surface ligands and receptors disrupts tumor–T cell interactions, conferring resistance to cytotoxic T cell killing, while on the Wnt co-receptor LRP6, polylactosamine extension promotes plasma membrane trafficking and enhances Wnt/β-catenin signalling [PMID:35338135, PMID:36980204].

DNAH14 encodes an axonemal dynein heavy chain containing an AAA+ ATPase motor domain that powers motile cilia and sperm flagellar beating. Dnah14 knockout mice exhibit subfertility due to reduced flagellar beat amplitude without morphological defects, and increasing sperm concentration during IVF partially rescues fertilization, demonstrating a specific role in flagellar waveform regulation rather than structural integrity [PMID:bio_10.1101_2025.07.28.667185]. Human biallelic loss-of-function variants in DNAH14 are associated with neurodevelopmental disorders including seizures, developmental delay, microcephaly, and ataxia, as well as congenital hydrocephalus consistent with motile ciliopathy [PMID:35438214, PMID:26636390, PMID:41596228].

DNAJC22 is a J-domain-containing transmembrane co-chaperone that functions in clathrin-mediated endocytosis at the apical membrane of epithelial cells. Studies of the Drosophila ortholog Wurst demonstrate that DNAJC22 recruits Hsc70 and clathrin to the apical membrane, and loss of function results in defective respiratory-tube size control and failure of airway lumen liquid clearance [PMID:17558392]. Transcription of Dnajc22 is directly regulated by HNF4A through a conserved binding site validated across fly, zebrafish, and mammalian systems [PMID:28642491]. Specific mammalian substrates and cellular functions beyond its placement within the Hsp70 co-chaperone interaction network remain uncharacterized.

PPEF1 is a calcium-regulated serine/threonine protein phosphatase whose catalytic activity is controlled by a dual Ca²⁺-sensor auto-inhibitory mechanism: in the resting state, the extended-IQ motif blocks substrate access to the active site, while Ca²⁺ binding to both calmodulin (via an N-terminal IQ motif with nanomolar affinity) and to C-terminal EF-hand domains drives conformational rearrangements that unlock the catalytic cleft [PMID:40169586, PMID:12051765]. PPEF1 dephosphorylates PDCD5 at Ser-119, destabilizing PDCD5 and thereby suppressing p53-mediated apoptosis under genotoxic stress, as demonstrated by catalytic-dead mutant controls [PMID:28051100]. Despite its homology to Drosophila RDGC, vertebrate PPEF1 is dispensable for rhodopsin dephosphorylation and photoreceptor integrity, as shown by double-knockout mice with normal retinal function [PMID:11713293].

PRKAG3 encodes a muscle-specific regulatory γ3 subunit of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) that governs skeletal muscle glycogen homeostasis and fibre-type composition. The dominant gain-of-function R200Q/R225Q substitution causes constitutive excess glycogen accumulation by enhancing Akt–AS160–GSK3 signaling, increasing hexokinase activity, and accelerating post-exercise glycogen resynthesis, while shifting muscle fibres toward an oxidative phenotype with higher type IIA/IIX content [PMID:10818001, PMID:20028849, PMID:21435205, PMID:21622967]. In Schwann cells, PRKAG3 functions as a negative regulator of migration downstream of a hypoxia–miR-132 axis, where miR-132 directly targets the PRKAG3 3′-UTR [PMID:26399639].

PSG7 is a secreted immunoglobulin superfamily glycoprotein with an N-A1-A2-B2-C domain architecture, encoded within a tandemly arrayed PSG gene cluster on chromosome 19q13.2 [PMID:7851895, PMID:2328001]. Its N-domain contains a conserved RGD motif in the CDR3-equivalent region shared with most PSG family members, and its C-terminal domain harbors a cysteine residue that may permit dimerization [PMID:2328001, PMID:1572651]. PSG7 transcription is activated during cytotrophoblast differentiation into syncytiotrophoblast under control of its 5′ regulatory region, and its secretion is upregulated by the inflammatory cytokines TNFα and IL-6, though direct effects on endothelial cell function are limited [PMID:20116096, PMID:35322669].

TEKT5 is a tektin-family intermediate-filament-like protein that localizes to the lumen of axonemal doublet microtubules in mammalian sperm flagella, where cryo-electron tomography reveals it forms an extensive crosslinking network with CCDC105 and SPACA9 to modulate flagellar mechanical properties [PMID:37865089]. Despite its structural role—Tekt5-knockout sperm exhibit flagellar deformities with 180° bends—genetic ablation does not abolish male fertility or sperm motility, indicating functional divergence from other tektins such as TEKT1 [PMID:37865089, PMID:41764189]. In ovarian cancer cells, TEKT5 knockdown causes G1 arrest and apoptosis through upregulation of HDAC6, loss of acetylated α-tubulin, nuclear accumulation of SMAD3, and consequent p27kip1 induction, placing TEKT5 as a negative regulator of HDAC6 that maintains tubulin acetylation and cell cycle progression [PMID:31208979].
